desc:
An AI lead handling and routing workflow reads each new enquiry, scores it by rules you can read and sends it to the right salesperson. Ecom Swift LLC builds it in your own CRM and tools, so no good lead waits in an inbox.

## What is lead handling?

Lead handling is everything that happens between a new enquiry arriving and a person starting a real conversation. It includes capturing the details, removing duplicates, deciding how promising the lead is, choosing who should follow up and sending a first reply. An automated workflow does the repeatable parts in seconds and leaves the conversation to your team.

The scoring rules are written in plain words that you approve, such as "asked for a quote" or "company has a team of ten or more". Nothing is hidden in a black box.

## Why slow lead response loses business

People who send an enquiry usually contact several businesses. The first company to answer sensibly tends to start the conversation. Leads that arrive on a weekend, land in the wrong inbox or sit beside spam wait too long, and interest fades.

Manual handling also creates uneven treatment. One enquiry gets a thoughtful reply, another gets none because the person who saw it was busy. Without a clear score, the best prospects look the same as casual browsers.

## How the workflow improves results

Faster, more consistent responses give more leads a chance to become customers. Salespeople spend time on prospects who match your criteria, and receive a short summary with the details they need, so the first call is informed. Lower-scoring leads are not ignored. They get a polite first reply or a nurture email, which keeps the door open without using up sales time.

A weekly summary shows which sources send useful leads, so you can put effort where it pays off. Actual results depend on your offer, your pricing and how quickly your team follows up.

## What a good lead flow includes

- Connections to each lead source, such as web forms, store enquiries and a shared inbox.
- Key details pulled out and saved in your CRM or sheet.
- A duplicate check, so one person does not appear three times.
- Score rules written in plain language.
- Routing to the correct salesperson by region, product or size.
- A short summary attached to each lead.
- A first reply drafted for review, or a nurture email for low scores.
- Follow-up reminders when a lead has not been contacted.
- A weekly summary of leads by source and score.

## What we do

We begin by listing where your leads come from and what a good lead looks like. Together we write the score rules and the routing rules. Then we build the connections, the sorting steps and the reply drafts in your CRM or spreadsheet. We run the flow against your real past leads and compare the results with your own judgment.

The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in the number of sources, rules and people routed to, and in reminders and reporting. We finish with a handover guide that explains how to change a rule yourself.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Start with a small set of simple score rules.
- Tell the workflow who covers for whom when someone is away.
- Review the first batch of scores against your own view.
- Keep reply drafts short and honest about next steps.
- Check the weekly summary and adjust rules.

**Avoid:**
- Scoring on details that tell you nothing, such as the time of day.
- Sending automatic replies that promise things you cannot deliver.
- Buying or scraping contact lists without permission.
- Routing every lead to one overloaded person.
- Leaving lower-scoring leads with no reply at all.

## Who it is for

A service business that receives quote requests through a website form and a phone-friendly inbox can use it. A store that gets wholesale enquiries mixed with ordinary support mail can separate them. A small sales team that shares leads informally can add clear ownership.

## What we need from you

Send a description of your best and worst past leads, the list of sources and the names of the people who should receive them. Tell us which CRM or sheet you use. We never need passwords. You add us as a collaborator or limited team user, and every connection is made in accounts you own.
